name: Mir iskusstva book graphics
summary: A firm, even black pen outline, in the manner of a woodcut, is filled with flat watercolour tints. The key line and the tints print in separate runs. Folk ornament frames each page.

philosophy.core_thesis: A single firm line and flat tints, set inside an ornamental frame, make a fairy-tale page that reads as a unit with its border and letters.
design_principles: Draw the outline with a pen in one even weight of about 0.4–0.6 mm at print size; do not swell or taper it.
Fill each area with one flat tint, with no shading; use 3–6 tints from a set of vermilion, Prussian blue, ochre and green.
Treat wood, fur, cloth and water as repeated patterns of short strokes inside the contour.
Frame each picture with a border of folk ornament, and draw the title letters by hand to match.
Draw the picture, the border and the text block as one page.
Print the black line as the key and the tints as separate runs; keep the register within 0.5 mm.
Use a smooth cream paper that shows the flat colour without a texture.
anti_patterns: Shaded or modelled forms and a gradient
A sketchy, loose line of changing weight
A picture with no border and no hand lettering
A bright white or coated glossy sheet

process.matrix: A zinc plate or a stone for the black key line, and a stone for each tint.
process.press: A flatbed lithographic press at a state printing works, with one run for each colour.
process.image_making: The artist draws the outline in ink and paints a colour guide in watercolour. A craftsman separates the tints and draws each one on its own stone.
process.edition: Thousands of copies of a tale book; the copies match.

inks.strategy: Black key line plus a set of flat, transparent tints that overprint where two meet.

colours.name: Black
colours.role: the contour, the pattern strokes and the letters

colours.name: Vermilion
colours.role: flat tint for cloth and accents

colours.name: Prussian blue
colours.role: flat tint for sky, water and cloth

colours.name: Ochre
colours.role: flat tint for gold and wood

colours.name: Green
colours.role: flat tint for plants and cloth

screening.rule: Make no tone. Fill each area with one flat tint inside the line, and use the bare paper for light.

registration.rule: The tints register to the key line within 0.5 mm. Print each tint under the line, or let it overlap the line by 0.3 mm.

substrate.stock: A smooth book paper, cream, with a hard surface for fine lines.
substrate.finish: Smooth and matt or with a light coat; the paper yellows at the edge.

surface.impression: No bite; a thin, flat film of ink on the surface.
surface.sheen: Matt to satin; the black is dense and the tints are soft.
surface.texture: Clean, even lines and flat tints with a slight grain from the stone.

marks: small tint gaps at line edges
tint overlap that makes a third colour

evidence.title: Illustration for the book Under the Arches

emotion.target_response: Ordered wonder: the viewer enters a fairy tale that is drawn with care, framed like an icon and calm in its colour.

avoid_when: The picture needs depth, shading or a modern look.
The line must be loose, rough or hand-sketched.

modifiers.how: Cut the outline in thick wood lines, let the hand colour shift from the line, and drop the ornamental border.
Use dense black fills and Baroque capitals; keep one flat red or ochre tint.

screen_ruling.note: The style makes no tone; the screen stays at zero.
